status: pre-registered before any paid call; not run
approval: No paid judge call runs until Eric approves the SHA-256 of this exact file. A change to any bound file below requires a new manifest and a new approval.
question: Does splitting a multi-sentence human message into one rule per kept sentence, with per-sentence replace/withdraw targets drawn from the newest 16 active rules plus the 16 most word-relevant older ones, keep rule-add accuracy at the 0.8 cutoff?

cases.provenance: Fresh synthetic messages authored by the agent for this run; no real chat text; none repeats an earlier rules case (checked against evals/rules/cases/synthetic.jsonl); no secret-like text (evals/recall SECRET_LIKE). Every case is split test, so the runner writes no traces.
cases.labelling: Eric's 2026-10-19 boundary: a rule is a standing instruction meant to hold beyond the current task; task-scoped instructions, recurring in-task instructions and one-off authorizations are not rules. A message with several sentences lists in gold.keep the sentences that state the rule, including an exception stated in its own sentence; gold.supersedes names the offered rule a message replaces.

scorer.note: Frozen and unchanged from c3efa48. It grades one decision per message. The candidate runner grades its per-sentence changes through messageDecision (evals/rules/run.ts): kept sentences joined in source order, a replacement if any sentence replaced, so both arms are scored by the same function on the same message-level outcome.

baseline.label: B
baseline.description: Joined rule text, newest-32 targets (rules.ts identical to v0.14.0).

candidate.label: C
candidate.revision: the Milestone 1 commit, recorded in the run report; its bound files must hash exactly as listed
candidate.description: One rule per kept sentence; per-sentence r<k>/x<k> targets over the newest 16 plus 16 most relevant active rules.

judge.role: the host judge role (openrouter/~typesafe/jev-latest), through evals/recall/judge.ts openHostJudge
judge.sameModel: Every result row of both arms must name the same served judge model; otherwise the run is INCONCLUSIVE.

budget.note: Judge spend only, from the host's reported usage. A row with unknown cost makes the run INCONCLUSIVE. The runner checks the ceiling before each attempt, so concurrent attempts can overshoot a per-arm ceiling by a few calls; the two per-arm ceilings together stay at the $0.50 cap.

procedure: Verify the sha256 of the case file and of every bound file of both arms (baseline from an ovnfs checkout at the baseline revision, candidate from the Milestone 1 commit). Any mismatch stops the run before a call.

B, from the baseline checkout: bun evals/rules/run.ts --variant baseline --cases <repo>/evals/rules/cases/atomic-20261106.jsonl --reps 3 --concurrency 4 --max-judge-calls 200 --max-cost-usd 0.25 --rule-add 0.8 --out <repo>/evals/rules/runs/atomic-20261106/baseline

C, from the candidate commit: bun evals/rules/run.ts --variant v1 --cases evals/rules/cases/atomic-20261106.jsonl --reps 3 --concurrency 4 --max-judge-calls 200 --max-cost-usd 0.25 --rule-add 0.8 --out evals/rules/runs/atomic-20261106/v1
Run B then C in the same session. A rerun only fills errored slots of the same out directory; no case, arm or setting changes after data.

metrics.primary: Rule-add F1 per arm over all result rows (51 cases x 3 repetitions), from grade.ts summarize: a row is a predicted add when the message's outcome adds or replaces any rule.
metrics.falsePositives: Per gold-none case, the number of repetitions with a predicted add.

adoptionRule: Adopt C (ship Milestone 1) iff both hold: (1) F1(C) >= F1(B) - 0.06, where 0.06 is the rules eval's measured baseline noise (test score 0.918 +/- 0.060, .omp/ratchet/rules-triage/narrative.md, used here as the F1 tolerance); and (2) no new false positives: for every gold-none case, C's false-positive repetitions are at most B's. Otherwise C is not adopted and Milestone 1 does not ship.
inconclusive: Not adopted, and reported as inconclusive rather than as a failure, if: either arm has error rows for more than 5% of its 153 slots after the runner's retries; any row has unknown cost; the served judge model differs between rows; or spend reaches the $0.50 cap before both arms finish. No relaxation after data.
secondaryReadouts: Reported, decide nothing: pass rate (score) per arm and per category; on gold-rule cases with several kept sentences, how often C wrote one change per kept sentence (results.jsonl changes); the two supersede-old cases, whose target (r3, r5) lies outside B's newest-32 offer. The message-level grader cannot tell whether a split-off exception sentence still reads correctly on its own; that is not measured here.

preflight.cost: $0, no judge calls (oracle and null modes, 1 repetition)
preflight.baselineOracle: 49/51 pass, F1 1.000; fails only atomic-supersede-old-01 and -02 (target not among the newest 32 offered)
